issues.description: The UML/problem description defines numberOfInscribedStudents as an int, but the solution implementation declares numberOfInscribedStudents as a long. This mismatch also causes the solution's getTotalNumberOfStudents() (declared to return int in the UML) to sum a long and an int, producing a long expression that cannot be returned as int without a cast — creating a compilation/semantic inconsistency and confusing students about the expected type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfInscribedStudents consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution to declare numberOfInscribedStudents as int (matching the UML/problem) and ensure constructor/getters/setters use int, or update the UML/problem to specify long and change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long (and update tests/documentation accordingly). Ensure the return type of getTotalNumberOfStudents matches the summed types to avoid narrowing and compilation errors.
